verdicts.explanation: The 2.62 x 10-4 S cm-1 value for the Nb2CTx MXene PEO/LiTFSI membrane is stated in the text as attributed to Liu et al. [105], and the paper gives no temperature for it, so null is correct. The 60 °C in the text refers to the transference number.

The 4.9 x 10-4 S cm-1 value is for the PEO/PGA/Al2O3/LiTFSI/Py13TFSI CPE from Li et al. [106]. Table 2 gives this conductivity at 50 °C, which supports the temperature, and solution casting is stated for this work.
The text says 'At 60 °C ... 5.27 x 10-4 S cm-1' for the PEO/LiTFSI/In2O3 CPE from Zhang et al. [110], and Table 2 agrees. In2O3 is a filler, so the empty dopants list is correct.

The text states ~2.7 x 10-4 S cm-1 at room temperature for the PEGDME/TEGDME-plasticized PVDF-HFP GPE from Castillo et al. [114], so null temperature is correct. Table 2 lists a different value (~2.7 x 10-3) for the same system, a discrepancy the record notes, but the text value is what the paper reports for this material.
The text reports a room-temperature ionic conductivity of up to 3.6 x 10-4 S cm-1 for the PVDF-HFP/LiTFSI/UCPBA CPE from Zhu et al. [42], and Table 2 agrees.
The 5.54 x 10-4 S cm-1 value for the NH2-MIL-53(Al) composite is attributed to Wang et al. [36] and is stated without a measurement temperature, so null is correct.
The text says 'At 30 °C, the ionic conductivity of ... PTMG-HDI-BHDS/LiFSI was measured to be 2.4 × 10− 4 S cm− 1', attributed to Pei et al. [120], and Table 2 agrees.

The text reports 1.10 × 10−5 S cm−1 at 25 °C for the Hu et al. [125] PEO semi-IPN electrolyte, which was prepared by in-situ cross-linking. The record's section label is slightly off but the values and origin are correct.
The text reports 1.41 × 10−4 S cm−1 at 60 °C for the same Hu et al. [125] electrolyte, so the value, temperature and literature origin are correct.

The text states 'an ionic conductivity of 7.8 x 10-4 S cm-1 at 25 °C' for the BPSO/PVDF/LiTFSI/cellulose acetate CPE from Chen et al. [124], and the Figure 6 caption confirms solution casting. Table 2 lists a different value (4.0 x 10-4), a discrepancy that does not change the text-based record.
The text reports 'ionic conductivity to 2.07 × 10−4 S cm−1 at 60 °C' for the quaternary-ammonium cellulose acetate nanofiber PEO electrolyte from Ji et al. [112].
